passages.original: 741-742 Magnum est quidem, amice, quod postulas, ut Origenem faciam Latinum, et hominem juxta Didymi videntis sententiam, alterum post Apostolum [Al. apostolos], Ecclesiarum magistrum etiam Romanis auribus donem. Sed oculorum, ut ipse nosti, dolore cruciatus, quem nimia impatiens lectione contraxi, et notariorum penuria, quia te- nuitas hoc quoque subsidium abstulit, quod recte cupis, tam ardenter ut cupis, implere non valeo.
passages.english: It is indeed a great thing that you ask, my friend: that I make Origen Latin, and present to Roman ears as well the man who, in the judgement of Didymus the seer, is the second teacher of the Churches after the Apostle. But, as you yourself know, I am tormented by a pain in my eyes, which I brought on through excessive and unrestrained reading, and by a lack of secretaries, since my poverty has taken away this help too; so what you rightly desire I am unable to fulfil as ardently as you desire it.
passages.notes: "741-742" at the start is a column reference from the printed edition and is omitted. "Didymi videntis": Didymus the Blind, called "the seer" here, apparently as a play on his blindness. The edition gives the variant "apostolos" ("after the apostles") for "Apostolum". "nimia impatiens lectione" is construed as "through excessive reading, impatient [of restraint]"; the exact force of "impatiens" is uncertain. "te- nuitas" is a word split by the scan, read as "tenuitas" (poverty).
